Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family holiday is approaching, which is a traditional time for everyone to reconnect.
Situation2: They must follow strict procedures for a large cash deposit at the end of a busy shift to comply with corporate auditing rules.
Story: The store was buzzing with the last-minute rush before the holiday. As a cashier, I knew the end-of-shift deposit was coming, and the manager had reminded us—no shortcuts, no delays, every bill counted and logged. I glanced at the clock, feeling the weight of the cash drawer in my hands. My phone vibrated in my pocket. It was a message from my daughter: “Grandpa, are you joining the family call? The kids can’t wait to see you!” My heart squeezed. Every year, this holiday call was our tradition, a time to laugh and reconnect, and I knew how much it meant to them—and to me. But the deposit process was strict, and if I left it incomplete, I’d be breaking store policy, risking my job and letting my team down. I stood there, torn, the cash in one hand and my phone in the other, feeling the pull of two worlds that both needed me, each with its own set of rules and expectations.
